sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Luimbi appears only as 'Lu-imbi (86 c)', a vocabulary from Fr. Keeling (p. 799). No Luimbi-specific accent remark. The front-matter transcription convention says only, for Bantu generally: 'The accent or pitch of the voice is indicated by '. This is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable than the penultimate.' -- a pan-Bantu convention, not a statement about Luimbi.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Group W (Luena, Mbunda, Lujazi/Ngangela incl. Luimbi, Nkoya, Cokwe) discussion pp. 99-100 covers prefixes, numerals, pronouns only; nothing on accent for Lujazi/Luimbi.
Luimbi article has no phonology; Luchazi article's stress-related vowel-length remarks come from Pearson's unpublished 'Luchazi Grammar' (K13), not Luimbi.
